# 1B.8 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024

**Bottom line:** The 2024 record is **mostly positive** for 1B.8. Scholz repeatedly chose de-escalatory language in acute crises, kept Germany’s Ukraine policy legible, and avoided rhetoric that would heighten accidental-war risk. The main negative item is the March 2024 Taurus communications leak, which exposed a real security-channel failure under his government. I found **no direct evidence** that Scholz intentionally preserved a special crisis channel with Russia in the classic hotline sense; the support here is therefore mostly indirect.

## Accepted claim items

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **Scholz im Interview mit der taz** | Bundesregierung | 13 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/scholz-interview-in-der-taz-2270696 | Scholz said fear of escalation is understandable, rejected a quick endgame by force, and framed support for Ukraine as necessary to prevent Russian victory. This is strong 1B.8 evidence because it explicitly prioritizes de-escalation in a live war context. | 1B.8, 1B.1 |
| **Scholz bei der Münchner Sicherheitskonferenz** | Federal Government | 17 Feb 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/speech-by-federal-chancellor-olaf-scholz-at-the-munich-security-conference-2260378 | Scholz emphasized credible deterrence, said Germany and its partners did not want a conflict between Russia and NATO, and reiterated that no German troops would be sent to Ukraine. This is clear crisis communication aimed at reducing accidental-war risk. | 1B.8, 1B.2, 1B.1 |
| **Questions orales au gouvernement mars 2024** | Bundesregierung | 4 Mar 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-fr/service/archives/chancelier-questions-2024-2265010 | Scholz said Taurus would require German soldiers to be involved and refused because he did not want Germany drawn into the war. That is direct evidence of a decision designed to preserve escalation control and avoid accidental involvement. | 1B.8, 1B.1, 1B.5 |
| **Bundeskanzler Scholz zur aktuellen Sicherheitslage** | Bundesregierung | 6 Jun 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/scholz-sicherheitslage-2291096 | Scholz said German security authorities had carefully prepared for a high-risk summer and framed safety as a core state duty. This supports the “communicate clearly and prepare calmly” side of 1B.8, though it is more domestic than international crisis management. | 1B.8, 1B.3 |
| **Rede von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz** | Bundesregierung | 5 Sep 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/rede-von-bundeskanzler-olaf-scholz-2307114 | Scholz described IRIS-T air defense as a safety measure that protects lives by intercepting rockets, drones, and cruise missiles. This is a clear example of framing military action as defensive and war-preventive rather than escalatory. | 1B.8, 1B.3 |
| **Le gouvernement fédéral s’efforce de parvenir à une désescalade** | Bundesregierung | 15 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-fr/service/archives/declaration-chancelier-iran-2270888 | After Iran’s attack on Israel, Scholz and the German government emphasized de-escalation and avoiding a regional conflagration. This is strong evidence that in a fast-moving crisis he chose public restraint rather than escalation signaling. | 1B.8 |
| **Bundestag statement on the European Council and NATO summit** | Federal Government | 26 Jun 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/regierungserklaerung-von-bundeskanzler-olaf-scholz-2294518 | Scholz discussed multiple crises and security needs without apocalyptic nuclear language or reckless threat framing. This supports a general pattern of careful crisis communication. | 1B.8, 1B.2 |
| **Germany and Russia spar over a leaked audio on missiles for Ukraine. Berlin promises to investigate** | AP | 4 Mar 2024 | https://apnews.com/article/russia-germany-ukraine-taurus-missiles-recording-de408772f1edf3bd2f98fd5a3f64da3c | Germany’s defense ministry treated the intercepted Taurus discussion as a security incident, said it would investigate, and planned to better counter targeted disinformation. This is the main negative item: a real communications-security failure increased accidental-war and misperception risk. | 1B.8, 1B.3 |
| **A German military officer used an unsecured line for a conference call. Russia hacked and leaked it** | AP | 5 Mar 2024 | https://apnews.com/article/germany-russia-ukraine-leaked-audio-taurus-98ba4fe85caf7d29902691f543a4dd04 | AP reported that an officer used an unsecured line, that overall security had been increased afterward, and that disciplinary review was considered. This shows a concrete lapse followed by corrective action, but not a failure of Scholz to de-escalate publicly. | 1B.8, 1B.3 |

## Counterevidence / limitations

- The **Taurus leak** is the strongest negative evidence for 1B.8 because it exposed a genuine communications-security weakness.
- I did **not** find direct evidence of Scholz maintaining a formal Russian-German crisis hotline or similar channel in 2024.
- I also did **not** find evidence that he escalated in crisis moments; the record is overwhelmingly restraint-oriented.

## Synthesis for 1B.8

- **Most supported reading:** Scholz generally de-escalated, communicated clearly, and avoided actions that would raise accidental-war risk.
- **Why:** he repeatedly rejected direct German involvement, used sober language around Ukraine and Iran, and framed defense measures as preventive.
- **Main caveat:** a real military communications breach undercut the ideal of perfect crisis discipline.
- **Overall:** positive on 1B.8, with one notable operational-security blemish and limited direct evidence about preserved cross-border crisis channels.
